claim: A wrench-conditioned Transformer diffusion model that reconstructs simulated Zero-Force Trajectories, combined with online directional impedance adaptation, enabled successful contact-rich manipulation on the reported KUKA LBR iiwa tasks; however, evidence for stable or safe interaction is conditional because stiffness increases toward baseline at nonzero displacement are not generally passive.
claim_locator: method description: diffusion-based sZFT reconstruction and SLERP scheduling
method description: energy-based online directional stiffness/damping adaptation
epistemic_status: author-reported experimental evidence with explicit stability limitations; broader generalization remains unverified
problem_and_setting: Learning compliant behavior for contact-rich manipulation from demonstrations while retaining a fixed nominal Zero-Force Trajectory and adapting impedance online. Demonstrations comprised Apple Vision Pro teleoperation parkour and robot-assisted-therapy data; evaluation used a torque-controlled KUKA LBR iiwa on parkour traversal and previously unseen cylindrical, square, and star peg-in-hole geometries.
method_or_mechanism: A Transformer diffusion model cross-attends to measured external wrenches and reconstructs simulated Zero-Force Trajectories, with quaternion orientation scheduled using SLERP. An energy-based estimator then adjusts diagonal directional stiffness and damping online while the nominal ZFT remains fixed. The controller reduces impedance in interaction directions and can restore gains toward a programmed baseline.
content_summary: Training used 1.6 hours and 72,000 demonstration samples and contained no peg-in-hole examples. In parkour testing, fixed impedance stopped at the first obstacle whereas the learned system traversed smoothly. Across 30 trials per peg geometry, diffusion plus directional adaptation achieved 100% success for cylindrical, square, and star pegs. Diffusion without directional adaptation achieved 0% for every geometry; directional adaptation without diffusion achieved 100% for the cylinder but 0% for square and star. Reported offset robustness was approximately ±3 mm for cylinder and square and ±1 mm for star. Baseline gains were chosen by an experienced programmer after testing 15 combinations. The output stiffness is restricted to diagonal positive-semidefinite matrices. Stiffness reduction is dissipative and passive with passive environments, but restoring stiffness toward baseline at nonzero displacement is not generally passive; strict passivity would require combination with passive impedance shaping.
synthesis_role: Provides empirical evidence that diffusion-reconstructed motion intent and directional impedance adaptation are complementary for contact-rich manipulation, while defining an important passivity boundary that limits unconditional stability and safety claims.
development_link: Extends demonstration-based impedance learning by separating wrench-conditioned sZFT reconstruction from online directional gain adaptation; motivates coupled-stiffness models, systematic architecture comparisons, broader task and baseline-gain validation, dual-arm evaluation, and passive impedance shaping for strict passivity.

evidence.finding: Training comprised 1.6 hours and 72,000 samples from teleoperated parkour and robot-assisted-therapy demonstrations, with no peg-in-hole training data.
Fixed impedance stopped at the first obstacle, while the full learned system traversed the parkour smoothly.
The full diffusion-plus-directional-adaptation system achieved 100% success for cylindrical, square, and star geometries.
Diffusion without directional adaptation achieved 0% for all three geometries; directional adaptation without diffusion achieved 100% for cylinder and 0% for square and star.
Tolerance was reported at approximately ±3 mm for cylindrical and square pegs and ±1 mm for the star peg.
An experienced programmer selected baseline gains after evaluating 15 combinations.

Stiffness reduction is dissipative and passive with passive environments, but increasing stiffness toward baseline at nonzero displacement is not generally passive; passive impedance shaping is proposed to enforce strict passivity.

boundary_conditions: Experiments used a torque-controlled KUKA LBR iiwa.
Peg-in-hole evaluation covered three geometries with 30 trials per geometry.
Training and deployment retained the same programmed baseline impedance; robustness to substantially different baseline settings was not tested.
Learned stiffness was diagonal and positive-semidefinite, excluding coupled stiffness terms.
The 1 N/1 Nm interaction threshold is sensor-specific and adjustable.
Passivity of stiffness reduction assumes a passive environment.
Stiffness restoration toward baseline is not generally passive when displacement is nonzero.
No systematic comparison against alternative model architectures was reported.
Evidence does not yet cover substantially wider tasks, environments, or dual-arm manipulation.
assumptions: Measured external wrenches are sufficiently accurate for conditioning and energy estimation.
The simulated Zero-Force Trajectory reconstruction is an adequate proxy for intended free-space motion.
The selected baseline impedance is appropriate for training and deployment.
The environment is passive when invoking the passivity argument for stiffness reduction.
Reported success percentages reflect the stated 30 trials per geometry.

reported: Fixed impedance stopped at the first parkour obstacle.
Diffusion without directional adaptation failed all peg-in-hole trials for all three geometries.
Directional adaptation without diffusion failed all square and star peg-in-hole trials.
Stiffness restoration toward baseline at nonzero displacement is not generally passive.
Robustness to substantially different baseline impedance settings was not tested.
Alternative architectures were not systematically compared.
Wider tasks, environments, and dual-arm scenarios remain unevaluated.
inferred: Perfect reported success rates may not generalize beyond the tested robot, geometries, offsets, baseline gains, and trial count.
Claims of generally stable or safe interaction would be unsupported without strict passivity enforcement or additional stability analysis during stiffness increases.
Baseline-gain selection by an experienced programmer after 15 combinations may introduce tuning dependence.

verification_status: verified only against the Controller-supplied full-text packet; no independent source or locator verification performed
